paragraphs: Answering questions about an image can require understanding how objects occupy three-dimensional space. An object’s orientation, the arrangement of its parts, and which objects hide others all matter. This paper introduces 3D-aware visual question answering to test that understanding, extending the emphasis of existing datasets and models beyond reasoning mainly about two-dimensional scenes.

The contribution combines a dataset with a model. Super-CLEVR-3D asks questions about parts, poses, and occlusions that require combining multiple pieces of spatial information. PO3D-VQA pairs neural networks using three-dimensional generative object representations with probabilistic neural-symbolic program execution. The recognition component supplies structured visual information, while the reasoning component uses it to work through the question.

In the reported experiments, PO3D-VQA substantially outperforms existing methods. However, performance still falls well short of that on two-dimensional VQA benchmarks. The results therefore show both the value of explicitly representing three-dimensional structure and the remaining difficulty of reasoning about it. The task exposes capabilities relevant to navigation and manipulation without establishing that those broader applications are solved.
neurips-2023-3d-aware-visual-question-an.tldr: A new dataset and model improve question answering about three-dimensional scenes while revealing substantial remaining challenges.

paragraphs: Active learning chooses which examples to request labels for, so its value depends on how much those choices reduce the labeling burden. In the agnostic setting, the learner must accommodate imperfect prediction. Some hypothesis classes and input distributions allow enormous savings over passive learning, while others offer little benefit. This paper seeks a guarantee that adapts to that variation.

The proposed algorithm competes with the best achievable query count for a given binary hypothesis class and input distribution. If some algorithm can reach error O(η) with m* queries, this algorithm reaches error of the same order using O(m* log H) queries. Its approach builds on splitting-based active learning, extending a style of guarantee previously obtained for the realizable setting.

The result measures performance against what is possible on the particular learning problem, rather than relying on the disagreement coefficient used by many existing algorithms. The paper also proves that improving the logarithmic overhead is NP-hard in general. Together, these results provide a competitive query guarantee and a computational obstacle to strengthening it universally.
neurips-2023-a-competitive-algorithm-for.tldr: A new agnostic active-learning algorithm achieves the target error with a logarithmic query overhead relative to the optimum.

paragraphs: An adversarial image created against one neural network may also fool another, enabling attacks when the target model is inaccessible. But this transfer often weakens because the image changes exploit details specific to the source network. The paper addresses that problem by changing the source model used to construct adversarial examples.

The Blurred-Dilated method reduces downsampling and introduces BlurPool and dilated convolutions into the source network. Adversarial samples are then generated using this modified model. The authors suggest that these changes preserve more feature information, allowing the attack to disrupt image features more thoroughly. That proposed explanation links the architectural modification to attacks that depend less on the original source model’s particular representations.

Experiments on ImageNet show significantly greater transferability than the state-of-the-art baselines considered. The method can also be combined with existing black-box attack techniques to improve their performance further. Its contribution is therefore a modification to the model used for attack generation that strengthens transfer in the reported evaluations, with feature preservation offered as the authors’ explanation for the improvement.
neurips-2023-blurred-dilated-method-for-.tldr: Modifying the source network with reduced downsampling, BlurPool, and dilated convolutions improves adversarial attack transfer on ImageNet.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning theory should help explain why deep learning succeeds in some environments and fails in others. This paper tests that connection using BRIDGE, a collection of 155 benchmark decision processes with tabular representations. Those representations let the authors compute problem-specific theoretical bounds exactly and compare them with practical algorithm performance.

Existing sample-complexity bounds correlate poorly with observed success. A more informative property concerns action rankings: deep RL tends to succeed when the best actions under the random policy’s Q-values are also optimal actions. The authors generalize this observation into the effective horizon. Roughly, it measures how far ahead search must look to identify the next optimal action when random rollouts evaluate the search endpoints.

Across four metrics on BRIDGE, bounds based on effective horizon reflect PPO and DQN performance more closely than previous bounds. The measure also predicts effects of reward shaping and a pretrained exploration policy that existing bounds miss. These findings make effective horizon a more empirically informative complexity measure in the studied environments, without turning the observed success pattern into an unconditional rule.
neurips-2023-bridging-rl-theory-and-prac.tldr: Effective horizon connects the lookahead needed for good decisions with observed deep reinforcement-learning performance more closely than prior bounds.

paragraphs: Large instruction-following language models can handle many tasks, but their computational demands make training, inference, and adaptation expensive. Access restrictions can also prevent customization. Cappy addresses these obstacles with a pretrained scorer containing 360 million parameters, designed to support task performance without requiring changes to a large model’s parameters.

Cappy has two roles. It can operate independently for classification or serve as an auxiliary component that improves a language model’s performance. Downstream supervision can be incorporated through Cappy without fine-tuning the associated language model or accessing its parameters. This creates an adaptation route for situations where direct model modification is impractical, while remaining compatible with fine-tuning and in-context learning.

On 11 PromptSource language-understanding tasks, standalone Cappy outperforms language models several orders of magnitude larger. On 45 complex BIG-Bench tasks, it substantially improves FLAN-T5 performance. The paper also reports additional gains when combining Cappy with other adaptation methods. These findings support a small scorer as both a capable classifier in the tested setting and a useful complement to larger multitask models.
neurips-2023-cappy-outperforming-and-boo.tldr: Cappy is a small pretrained scorer that performs classification and improves larger language models without requiring access to their parameters.

paragraphs: Learning a data distribution and answering causal questions require connecting observations to the process that produced them. This paper studies how normalizing flows can represent that causal process. Using recent results on nonlinear independent component analysis, it establishes identifiability from observational data given a causal ordering, and shows how autoregressive flows can recover the corresponding models.

The causal ordering is a central condition of that theoretical result. The paper then examines architectural and learning choices that help causal normalizing flows capture the underlying data-generating process. It also explains how to implement the do-operator within these models, enabling questions about interventions and counterfactual alternatives through an explicit causal representation.

Experiments assess design and training choices through an ablation study and compare causal flows with other causal-model approximation approaches. They also demonstrate applications involving mixed discrete and continuous data and only partial knowledge of the causal graph. The contribution connects a conditional identification result with practical modeling choices and causal-query procedures, while empirically exploring settings that complicate real-world use.
neurips-2023-causal-normalizing-flows-fr.tldr: The paper connects causal identification given an ordering with normalizing-flow designs for intervention and counterfactual reasoning.

paragraphs: Conditional independence testing asks whether variables remain related after accounting for other information. Many modern tests first train predictive models, then use those predictions in a statistical test. Their guarantees against false positives depend on accurately learning the required regression functions or Bayes predictors. This paper examines what happens when that intermediate learning step goes wrong.

The failure can arise because the model family lacks sufficient flexibility or because training does not produce the desired predictor. The authors describe these problems as misspecified inductive biases. For three regression-based tests, they derive new approximations or upper bounds for testing errors that explicitly depend on prediction misspecification. This connects weaknesses in the learned predictor to the reliability of the subsequent statistical conclusion.

The paper also introduces the Rao-Blackwellized Predictor Test, designed to be robust against these misspecified biases. Experiments on artificial and real data demonstrate the usefulness of both the analysis and the proposed method. The contribution makes prediction error part of the testing analysis and offers a test intended to tolerate it more effectively.
neurips-2023-conditional-independence-te.tldr: The paper analyzes how misspecified predictors affect conditional independence tests and introduces a test robust to such misspecification.

paragraphs: Changing how papers are assigned to reviewers may change review quality, but evaluating an alternative policy requires reasoning about assignments that were not made. This paper uses randomness already introduced into reviewer assignment to mitigate fraud. Because randomized policies can select many different reviewer-paper matches, their resulting reviews provide evidence about alternative assignment policies.

Some matches still have no chance of appearing, creating violations of the positivity requirement used in standard off-policy evaluation. The authors address this with partial-identification methods, which constrain possible outcomes using monotonicity and Lipschitz smoothness assumptions linking reviewer-paper characteristics to review outcomes. These assumptions support evaluation where the observed assignments alone do not fully identify the alternative policy’s effect.

The methods are applied to TPDP’21 and AAAI’22 review data. The analysis examines assignment weights and the quality cost of randomization. It finds higher review quality when textual similarity receives more weight, and only a marginal quality reduction from randomization. The findings inform these assignment choices, while the partial-identification approach may also be useful for other algorithmic matching systems.
neurips-2023-counterfactual-evaluation-o.tldr: Randomized reviewer assignments enable counterfactual policy evaluation, with reported evidence favoring text similarity and finding a small quality cost from randomization.

paragraphs: Learning from incorrectly labeled images often involves selecting examples whose labels appear trustworthy. Difficult but trustworthy examples near the classifier’s decision boundary can be especially important for generalization. This paper identifies one reason some examples are difficult: information about image style becomes entangled with the semantic content needed to distinguish classes.

CS-Isolate aims to infer content features that remain stable as style changes. Because clean content factors are not directly observed in noisy data, the method uses image augmentations to vary style and regularizes the inferred content using some confident examples. Its objective is to preserve content information for examples belonging to the same underlying clean class despite changes in their presentation.

The inferred content factors are then used to train existing noisy-label learning methods. Benchmark experiments show their effectiveness in learning hard examples. The approach matters because it targets the representation that makes an example seem ambiguous: separating style from content can make some difficult examples more discriminative and more useful for training, even when the supplied labels contain errors.
neurips-2023-cs-isolate-extracting-hard-.tldr: CS-Isolate separates inferred content from style to help noisy-label learning methods use difficult, trustworthy examples.

paragraphs: Hyperparameter choices can strongly affect a model’s performance, but optimizing them is difficult when hyper-gradients are unavailable. This situation can arise with discrete hyperparameters or nondifferentiable evaluation metrics. The paper studies this class of problems and proposes a method intended to improve convergence and avoid saddle points during the search.

The first step is stochastic relaxation, which makes gradient and Hessian information available without requiring the original hyper-gradients. The method then uses cubic regularization to exploit this curvature information. These two components work together: relaxation supplies information about how the optimization landscape changes, and cubic regularization uses it to guide the search beyond purely first-order behavior.

The authors prove convergence to approximate second-order stationary points, including when the lower-level optimization problem is solved inexactly. This is a stationarity guarantee rather than a guarantee of finding the global optimum. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate the method’s effectiveness. The contribution thus combines a way to obtain useful optimization information with a curvature-based procedure and a guarantee that accommodates imperfect inner solves.
neurips-2023-efficient-hyper-parameter-o.tldr: Stochastic relaxation and cubic regularization enable hyperparameter optimization with second-order convergence guarantees when hyper-gradients are unavailable.

paragraphs: Event-based vision data contain patterns across both space and time. Convolutional spiking neural networks can extract spatial structure effectively, but the paper argues that they overlook temporal features connecting successive time points. The proposed model adds recurrence and attention so that past information can contribute more selectively to recognizing the current pattern.

The architecture embeds a spiking convolutional block attention module, SCBAM, in a recurrent spiking neural network. This module adaptively accesses historical information through spatial and temporal channels. Its purpose is to combine useful spatial and sequential features while removing redundant history. The memory mechanism therefore concerns both which past information is useful and how efficiently that information can be retained and recalled.

Evaluation on DVS128-Gesture and other time-series datasets finds higher accuracy than the compared models while using less memory space. The reported results also indicate better use of history across spatial and temporal dimensions. The contribution is a recurrent attention design that improves the usefulness of stored history in these experiments, linking temporal modeling with more efficient memory use.
neurips-2023-enhancing-adaptive-history-.tldr: A spiking attention module helps a recurrent network use spatial and temporal history more accurately with less memory in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Spectral clustering groups data using a matrix of pairwise similarities. In a federated setting, those pairs may span data held in different locations, making direct similarity computation conflict with privacy constraints. This paper addresses that obstacle for unsupervised learning, where secure federated methods have received less attention than other learning tasks.

The proposed kernelized factorization method implicitly constructs an approximation to the similarity matrix for the distributed dataset. This approximation enables spectral clustering while respecting the method’s privacy constraints. The central idea is to reconstruct the information needed for clustering without directly building the full matrix from exposed cross-location data pairs.

The paper supplies several forms of theoretical support: convergence of the optimization algorithm, reconstruction-error bounds for a Gaussian kernel matrix, and a sufficient condition for correct clustering. It also presents differential-privacy results. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show efficient and accurate performance relative to the evaluated baselines. These findings connect the quality of the reconstructed similarities to clustering behavior, with correctness established under a sufficient condition rather than claimed for every dataset.
neurips-2023-federated-spectral-clusteri.tldr: Secure kernel approximation enables spectral clustering across distributed data, supported by convergence, reconstruction, and conditional clustering guarantees.

paragraphs: Multi-view clustering combines different views or modalities of data to discover groups without labels. Existing approaches often make restrictive assumptions about semantic consistency among samples. This paper reformulates the problem through information theory, providing a general model for learning representations and assigning samples to clusters within the same framework.

The authors express three desired properties—comprehensiveness, concentration, and cross-diversity—in terms of mutual information. They approximate high-dimensional mutual information to obtain a multi-view variational lower bound, creating a tractable objective for the model. Kullback–Leibler divergence is then used to derive sample assignments. Deep networks and Stochastic Gradient Variational Bayes bring these ingredients together for joint representation learning and clustering.

Experiments across varied synthetic and real datasets report more stable and better clustering performance than the state-of-the-art algorithms compared. The importance of the formulation is that it grounds multiple learning goals in one information-based objective and connects that objective to actual cluster assignments. The empirical results support the usefulness of this unified approach across the tested data types.
neurips-2023-generalized-information-the.tldr: An information-theoretic framework jointly learns multi-view representations and clusters, with improved stability and performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Privacy-preserving action recognition transforms videos to hide private information while retaining clues about the actions being performed. A difficult deployment problem is that privacy risks can change: new sensitive attributes or new attack models may appear after training. This paper develops a framework that trains for generalization along both of those dimensions.

The proposed Meta Privacy-Preserving Action Recognition framework uses meta-learning to simulate these changes during training. It constructs separate support and query sets that differ in privacy attributes or attack models. A virtual training-and-testing procedure then measures how learning on one set transfers to the other. That feedback guides the model toward handling the kinds of differences it may encounter later.

Experiments report improved effectiveness and generalization compared with state-of-the-art approaches. The key contribution is making unfamiliar attributes and unfamiliar attackers part of the training objective through simulated task shifts. This supports better adaptation to the tested privacy changes while preserving the action-recognition purpose of the transformed videos; the reported findings do not amount to universal protection against every possible future attack.
neurips-2023-joint-attribute-and-model-g.tldr: Meta-learning improves video anonymization’s generalization to privacy attributes and attack models absent during training.

paragraphs: Domain generalization aims to train models that work on a target domain unavailable during training. Adversarial approaches pursue this by learning features that look similar across source domains. This paper revisits the discrepancy measure used to encourage that similarity, arguing that a margin-based measure offers advantages over the commonly used measure based on binary disagreement.

MADG uses a margin-loss discrepancy to guide adversarial training across all source domains. Margins retain graded information about predictions, giving the discrepancy more information than a simple disagreement indicator. The paper motivates this choice as tighter, practical, and efficiently optimizable. The resulting training procedure seeks domain-invariant features that support performance on an unseen target.

The authors also derive a target-error generalization bound using margin loss and Rademacher complexity, linking source and unseen domains in a real-valued hypothesis space. Evaluations use DomainBed with VLCS, PACS, OfficeHome, DomainNet, and TerraIncognita, showing consistent performance across those datasets. The contribution combines a different adversarial training signal with theoretical analysis and broad benchmark evaluation; the abstract does not claim universal superiority across target domains.
neurips-2023-madg-margin-based-adversari.tldr: MADG uses margin-based adversarial learning to encourage domain-invariant features, supported by a generalization bound and consistent benchmark results.

paragraphs: Multi-armed bandit algorithms balance trying uncertain options against choosing those that currently look best. Upper Confidence Bound methods make this trade-off using optimistic estimates of rewards. Many such estimates require advance knowledge of a reward scale, such as a variance or payoff bound. The paper develops a data-dependent alternative that does not require that scaling information.

MARS, short for Maximum Average Randomly Sampled, constructs its upper confidence bound from the maximum average of randomly sampled rewards. It operates in a nonparametric setting with symmetric rewards. This replaces a scale-dependent confidence construction with one based on the observed reward data, addressing the concern that conventional bounds rely on limited tail information and a scale parameter supplied beforehand.

The authors derive a regret bound under the same assumptions used for the ψ-UCB method, without adding correction factors. Numerical experiments illustrate MARS and compare it with baseline algorithms. The contribution is a scale-free confidence construction with theoretical support, while symmetry of the rewards remains part of the stated setting rather than a property the method dispenses with.
neurips-2023-maximum-average-randomly-sa.tldr: MARS uses randomly sampled reward averages to build scale-free upper confidence bounds for stochastic bandits with symmetric rewards.

paragraphs: Visual tracking requires locating a target efficiently as new images arrive. Transformer trackers can be accurate, but their computational cost complicates GPU and CPU deployment. MixFormerV2 simplifies the tracking architecture by using a fully transformer framework without dense convolutional operations or a complex confidence-prediction module.

The model adds four prediction tokens to tokens representing the target template and search region. Mixed attention allows these tokens to capture relationships between the target’s appearance and candidate locations. Simple multilayer perceptron heads then predict the tracking box and its confidence. A two-part distillation procedure further reduces cost: dense-to-sparse distillation transfers knowledge from MixViT, while deep-to-shallow distillation supports removing backbone layers.

The paper presents two model sizes. MixFormerV2-B achieves 70.6% AUC on LaSOT and 56.7% on TNL2k at 165 GPU frames per second. MixFormerV2-S exceeds FEAR-L by the reported 2.7% AUC on LaSOT while running in real time on CPU. These results connect architectural simplification and distillation with useful accuracy and speed in the evaluated tracking settings.
neurips-2023-mixformerv2-efficient-fully.tldr: MixFormerV2 combines prediction tokens and model distillation to deliver accurate transformer tracking at high GPU and real-time CPU speeds.

paragraphs: Allocating indivisible items fairly is difficult because items cannot be split to balance everyone’s value precisely. This paper studies guarantees relative to each agent’s maximin share for fractionally subadditive, or XOS, valuations. In this setting, some instances prevent any allocation from giving every agent more than half of their maximin share.

For deterministic allocations, the authors improve the known guaranteed fraction from 0.219225 to 3/13, approximately 0.230769. Their allocation algorithm introduces new ways of handling large items. This strengthens the worst-case fairness guarantee for the stated valuation class, rather than claiming that every instance can achieve each agent’s full maximin share.

The randomized result combines two kinds of protection: an expected guarantee before the random allocation is drawn and a minimum guarantee for the allocation actually realized. The proposed scheme provides one-quarter of maximin share ex ante and one-eighth ex post. The paper also establishes an upper bound of three-quarters on the ex-ante guarantee for XOS valuations. Together, the results distinguish improvements available through randomization from limits on what such guarantees can promise.
neurips-2023-randomized-and-deterministi.tldr: The paper improves deterministic maximin-share fairness for XOS valuations and gives randomized guarantees both in expectation and after allocation.

paragraphs: A neural radiance field represents a scene through density and color fields. Matching training images does not ensure these fields separate shape and appearance correctly: different combinations can explain the same views. Existing regularizers address this ambiguity using general expectations that density should be smooth, sparse, or compact, which may not suit every scene.

This paper proposes a regularizer guided more directly by the observed images. Given a density field and images with known poses, it estimates the color field in closed form and then performs rendering. The method addresses occlusion and unevenly distributed viewpoints during color estimation. Because color is derived from density and observations, the resulting rendering supplies a way to evaluate and regularize the density field.

The supervision comes from photometric loss, making the regularization responsive to the particular scene rather than relying only on general density assumptions. Experiments report qualitative and quantitative improvements in NeRF density fields. The result supports reducing shape-radiance ambiguity through image-guided color estimation; it does not claim that fitting images alone uniquely determines the correct scene geometry.
neurips-2023-reducing-shape-radiance-amb.tldr: Closed-form color estimation supplies scene-adaptive supervision that improves NeRF density fields and reduces shape-radiance ambiguity.

paragraphs: A language model’s performance on familiar data may not predict how it handles a different distribution. This paper argues that many previous evaluations use insufficiently challenging shifts. It proposes a benchmark-construction protocol for clearer, harder distribution differences and introduces BOSS, covering five tasks and twenty datasets.

Using BOSS, the authors examine how ordinary fine-tuning links in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance. They identify three recurring relationship types that could potentially help forecast robustness as performance on familiar data improves. They also evaluate five established methods. Although those methods help in some cases, they do not provide significant improvement over ordinary fine-tuning in the reported evaluation.

The study then evaluates five large language models under different adaptation approaches. With enough in-distribution data, fine-tuned domain-specific models perform substantially better on familiar examples. For shifted examples, large models using in-context learning yield better results. Both model families still struggle with downstream tasks. These findings make the evaluation distribution central to model selection: strong familiar-data results and effective behavior under distribution shift can favor different approaches.
neurips-2023-revisiting-out-of-distribut.tldr: BOSS introduces harder NLP distribution shifts and reveals different strengths for fine-tuned domain models and large models using in-context learning.

paragraphs: Small changes to a text prompt can disrupt what a text-to-image model generates. This paper finds that the requested main subject may blend with another category or disappear, even when the subject’s category words remain intact. It introduces Auto-attack on Text-to-image Models, or ATM, to find such perturbations efficiently.

ATM is gradient-based, but replacing or adding words is ordinarily a discrete operation. The method learns a Gumbel Softmax distribution to make that search continuous and differentiable. Once learned, the distribution can produce multiple attack samples at the same time. This gives the method a way to search over prompt modifications while keeping the category keywords unchanged.

The reported attack success rates are 91.1% for short text and 81.2% for long text. Further empirical analysis identifies three patterns associated with the attacks: differences in generation speed, shared coarse characteristics, and words with multiple meanings. The findings expose a robustness weakness in the studied generation process: retaining the intended subject’s name does not reliably preserve that subject when surrounding prompt wording is perturbed.
neurips-2023-stable-diffusion-is-unstabl.tldr: ATM finds small prompt changes that can erase or distort intended image subjects without changing their category keywords.

paragraphs: An intervention can affect an outcome directly or indirectly through an intermediate process. Distinguishing these paths becomes harder when measurements arrive irregularly and treatment, mediators, and outcomes interact over time. This paper extends causal mediation modeling toward that healthcare setting, where static analyses and regularly sampled models can miss important temporal relationships.

The proposed nonparametric model assumes the mediator is a temporal point process interacting with the outcome process. This represents the mediator through events occurring over time and allows the model to address longer-range mediator–outcome interactions. The method estimates how an external intervention changes the future outcome trajectory through both direct and indirect pathways, rather than reducing the intervention’s effect to one static quantity.

On semi-synthetic data, the method accurately estimates direct and indirect effects. Applied to real healthcare data, it infers clinically meaningful trajectories for the direct and indirect effects on blood glucose after surgery. These results support the model’s usefulness for time-dependent mediation analysis, with the temporal point-process representation of the mediator serving as an explicit modeling assumption.
neurips-2023-temporal-causal-mediation-t.tldr: A temporal point-process mediation model estimates how direct and indirect intervention effects unfold across future healthcare outcomes.

paragraphs: Text-to-image diffusion models learn relationships between images and descriptions, but image generation alone does not reveal all the knowledge they contain. This paper probes that knowledge by using the models as zero-shot image classifiers. The goal is to turn their existing generative ability into a way of assessing candidate labels.

The method adds noise to an image and asks how well the diffusion model can remove it when conditioned on a textual label description. Denoising ability serves as a proxy for the label’s likelihood. Applied to Stable Diffusion and Imagen, this procedure lets the authors compare the models with CLIP and examine more specific aspects of their visual understanding.

The diffusion models perform competitively with CLIP across a broad range of zero-shot classification datasets. They also achieve state-of-the-art results on shape-versus-texture bias tests and succeed at attribute binding where CLIP fails in the reported evaluation. These results support exploring generative pretraining as an alternative for vision and vision-language tasks, extending its relevance beyond producing convincing images.
neurips-2023-text-to-image-diffusion-mod.tldr: Text-conditioned denoising lets diffusion models perform competitive zero-shot classification and reveal visual knowledge beyond image generation.

paragraphs: Adapting a text-to-image diffusion model for video editing can produce frames that fail to follow the prompt consistently or change unevenly over time. This paper attributes those problems to temporal-learning modules that shift the distribution of internal features. Its EI² model aims to preserve editing capability while improving consistency across frames.

The Shift-restricted Temporal Attention Module addresses that feature shift. The authors’ theoretical analysis links the shift closely to Layer Normalization, so the module replaces it with Instance Centering to preserve temporal feature distributions. It also uses attention with a normalized mapping to constrain changes in feature variance. These choices target the effects of adding temporal processing to a pretrained image model.

A second component, the Fine-coarse Frame Attention Module, uses spatial information at different levels of detail across the frames to further improve temporal consistency. Extensive experiments report superior performance for the combined EI² model. The contribution ties an identified feature-distribution problem to specific normalization and attention changes, then combines them with broader frame information to improve video-editing behavior.
neurips-2023-towards-consistent-video-ed.tldr: EI² improves diffusion-based video editing by restricting temporal feature shifts and combining fine and coarse information across frames.

paragraphs: Real visual data contain both unevenly represented categories and categories unknown during training. This paper combines those challenges in distribution-agnostic generalized category discovery. The task requires detailed predictions for both known and unknown classes in a long-tailed, open-world setting, extending beyond simply flagging unfamiliar examples as unknown.

The proposed BaCon framework has two collaborating branches: contrastive learning and pseudo-labeling. The contrastive branch estimates the data distribution and uses that information to regularize the pseudo-labeling branch’s predictions. In return, pseudo-labeling guides contrastive learning through self-balanced knowledge transfer and a new contrastive loss. Each branch therefore supplies supervision that helps the other address the combined discovery and imbalance problem.

The authors compare BaCon with methods from imbalanced semi-supervised learning and generalized category discovery. Across the evaluated datasets, it outperforms all compared baselines, with additional analysis supporting its effectiveness. The contribution is both a task formulation that brings imbalance and unknown categories together and a mutually supervising architecture designed for that setting. The reported advantage is empirical across the studied datasets.
neurips-2023-towards-distribution-agnost.tldr: BaCon combines contrastive learning and pseudo-labeling to discover known and unknown categories under class imbalance.
